curated-fs-telma-gf-noto-serif-vithkuqi: A high mean line runs through every word of Telma, its pen-written letters flowing with a wide-mouthed a. Noto Serif Vithkuqi follows as a classic serif, round-bowled and sturdy, steady enough for a longer read.
curated-fs-telma-gf-noto-serif-yezidi: Noto Serif Yezidi forms words as solid blocks, with strokes that taper gently. Telma's flowing, pen-written script sits above that density and loosens it, giving the page a graceful opening before the classic serif settles in.
curated-fs-telma-gf-orienta: Orienta keeps its letters open, with little gap between capitals and lowercase. Telma is at its best when its flowing script lines run loose and graceful, while Orienta does its best work when the text just needs to be clear.
curated-fs-telma-gf-radio-canada: That high mean line across every word gives Telma its quiet, pen-written look. Radio Canada, a sans-serif with tall, full curves and no pressure shifts, gives the script a firm, open partner underneath.
curated-fs-telma-gf-stack-sans-headline: Telma writes in flowing, understated script, say for a wedding website. Stack Sans Headline sits below as a monoline sans with wide gaps and a deep middle band, keeping the graceful lettering anchored and easy to follow.
curated-fs-telma-gf-voces: Voces reads tall and crisp, its stems and hairlines close in weight. Telma does its best work as a graceful, pen-written script with a high mean line, while Voces is built for steady, clear text.
curated-fs-telma-gf-winky-rough: Winky Rough has a body height that nearly matches its capitals. Telma's brush-like script adds slight pressure variation above it, though a longer passage in the sans would feel dense and wearing.
